SMTO-TSK-0006 — SMTO can't find this conversation

GUID: 7782604a-755d-4496-b2c6-2100d0ad68f6
Slug: conversation-not-found
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The conversation this action belongs to isn't available anymore. It may have been deleted, perhaps in another browser tab, or this page is showing an out-of-date list.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page in your browser so the conversation list is up to date. If the conversation was deleted in another tab or window, this page may still be showing it.
  2. Open the Conversations pane and select the conversation again. If you can't see it, type part of its title into Search conversations. Choosing it from the fresh list makes sure SMTO uses a conversation that still exists.
  3. If it isn't in the list, it was deleted. Select New chat and start the work again there. A deleted conversation can't be reopened, so the action needs a conversation that exists.

What success looks like

  • The conversation opens from the Conversations pane and your action goes through without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If a task in the missing conversation was changing files or other systems, check those yourself before redoing the work, because it may already have run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The server could not resolve the conversation or session for this request: the record is missing, deleted, abandoned or purged, no longer retained, or no conversation was supplied for a conversation-scoped action.

What this means

  • The selected conversation/session record is missing, deleted/tombstoned, out of the route's expected scope or absent from retained metadata. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The selected conversation/session record is missing, deleted/tombstoned, out of the route's expected scope or absent from retained metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh retained conversation/session history and check the exact identifier; absence does not imply external task effects were undone.

How to fix it

  • Find the rejected conversation_id in the Server log or Technical details and check whether that conversation was deleted, purged or abandoned. Reload the client so it drops the stale ID, and start new work in an existing or new conversation instead of resubmitting the old ID.
  • Refresh conversation history and select an existing conversation. Keep any retained task or artifact references for reconciliation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The action addresses an existing conversation in the supported retention scope.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
